v.en: O God, come to my assistance;

r.la: Et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.
r.en: And my mouth shall declare thy praise.

full.la: Hódie, si vocem Dómini audiéritis, * Nolíte obduráre corda vestra.
full.en: When you hear the voice of the Lord today * Do not harden your heart.

la: Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.

Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
Sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
en: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

v.la: Ne perdas cum ímpiis, Deus, ánimam meam.
v.en: Take not away my soul, O God, with the wicked.

r.la: Et cum viris sánguinum vitam meam.
r.en: Nor my life with bloody men.

text.la: Memor fuit in sǽculum * testaménti sui Dóminus Deus noster.
text.en: The memory of thy testament * will live forever, O Lord our God.

text.la: Auxit Dóminus * pópulum suum: et firmávit eum super inimícos eius.
text.en: The Lord increased his people exceedingly * and strengthened them over their enemies.

text.la: Edúxit Deus * pópulum suum in exsultatióne, et eléctos suos in lætítia.
text.en: The Lord brought forth * his people with joy, and his chosen with gladness.

text.la: Salvávit eos Dóminus * propter nomen suum.
text.en: The Lord saved them * for his own name's sake.

text.la: Oblíti sunt Deum * qui salvávit eos.
text.en: They forgot God * who saved them.

text.la: Cum tribularéntur * vidit Dóminus: et audívit oratiónem eórum.
text.en: And he saw when they were in tribulation * and he heard their prayer.

text.la: Clamavérunt ad Dóminum * et de necessitátibus eórum liberávit eos.
text.en: Then they cried to the Lord * and he delivered them out of their distresses.

text.la: Ipsi vidérunt * ópera Dei et mirabília eius.
text.en: These have seen * the works of the Lord, and his wonders.

text.la: Vidébunt recti * et lætabúntur, et intéllegent misericórdias Dómini.
text.en: The just see and rejoice * and understand the mercy of the Lord.

text.la: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
text.en: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

text.la: A vínculis peccatórum nostrórum absólvat nos omnípotens et miséricors Dóminus.
text.en: May the Almighty and merciful Lord loose us from the bonds of our sins.

benedictio.la: Evangélica léctio sit nobis salus et protéctio.
benedictio.en: May the Gospel's holy lection Be our safety and protection.

source.en: Continuation of the Holy Gospel according to John

text.la: In illo témpore: Cogitavérunt príncipes sacerdótum ut et Lázarum interfícerent: quia multi propter illum abíbant ex Iudǽis, et credébant in Iesum. Et réliqua. Homilía sancti Augustíni Epíscopi Tractatus 50 in Ioannem, in fine Viso Lázaro resuscitáto, quia tantum miráculum Dómini tanta erat evidéntia diffamátum, tanta manifestatióne declarátum, ut non possent vel occultáre quod factum est, vel negáre: quid invenérunt, vidéte. Cogitavérunt autem príncipes sacerdótum ut et Lázarum interfícerent. O stulta cogitátio, et cæca sævítia! Dóminus Christus, qui suscitáre pótuit mórtuum, non posset occísum! Quando Lázaro inferebátis necem, numquid auferebátis Dómino potestátem? Si áliud vobis vidétur mórtuus, áliud occísus: ecce Dóminus utrúmque fecit, et Lázarum mórtuum, et seípsum suscitávit occísum.
text.en: In that time, the chief priests thought to kill Lazarus also: Because many of the Jews, by reason of him, went away, and believed in Jesus. And so on. Homily by St. Augustine, Bishop 50th Tract on John When they saw Lazarus who had been raised from the dead, and knew that the miracle which the Lord had worked was so great, spread about by so many witnesses, and so plain and manifest that it could neither be concealed nor denied, they invented an expedient; and see here what it was: “But the chief Priests consulted that they might put Lazarus also to death.” What stupidity of thought, what blindness of cruelty is here! If the Lord Christ had raised up again a man who had died a natural death, could He not also raise up one that had died by violence? Would killing Lazarus paralyse the Lord? But if ye consider that there is a difference between a man dead of disease, and a man killed, behold, the Lord hath raised up both for He first raised up Lazarus, who had died a natural death, and then Himself, after a violent one.

body.la: Tota die contristátus ingrediébar, Dómine: quóniam ánima mea compléta est illusiónibus:
body.en: O Lord, I go mourning all the day long, for my soul is filled with a loathsome disease

refrain.la: Et vim faciébant, qui quærébant ánimam meam.
refrain.en: They also that sought after my life have used violence against me.

verse.la: Amíci mei et próximi mei advérsum me appropinquavérunt et stetérunt: et qui iuxta me erant, de longe stetérunt.
verse.en: My friends and my neighbours draw near, and stand over against me; and they that are nearest to me stand afar off.

benedictio.en: God's most mighty strength alway be His people's staff and stay.

source.la: In crástinum autem turba multa, quæ vénerat ad diem festum, cum audíssent quia venit Iesus Ierosólymam: accepérunt ramos palmárum, et processérunt óbviam ei, et clamábant: Hosánna, benedíctus qui venit in nómine Dómini, Rex Israël. Rami palmárum laudes sunt, significántes victóriam: quia erat Dóminus mortem moriéndo superatúrus, et trophǽo crucis de diábolo mortis príncipe triumphatúrus. Vox autem obsecrántis est Hosánna, sicut nonnúlli dicunt, qui Hebrǽam linguam novérunt, magis afféctum índicans, quam rem áliquam signíficans, sicut sunt in lingua Latína, quas interiectiónes vocant: velut cum doléntes dícimus, heu; vel cum delectámur, vah dícimus.
source.en: “On the next day much people that were come to the feast, when they heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem, took branches of palm-trees, and went forth to meet Him, and cried Hosanna! Blessed is the King of Israel That cometh in the Name of the Lord!” Palm branches are glorious boughs which tell of victory; yea, the Lord was now ready by His Own Death to trample down death, and to carry the victorious banner of His Cross in triumph over the devil, the prince of death. The cry with which He was greeted, namely “Hosanna,” hath not, as we are assured by some who are acquainted with the Hebrew language, any meaning in particular, but is a shout after the manner of interjections, as they are called, just as in Latin when we lament we say “Heu,” or when we are pleased, “Vah.”

body.la: Ne avértas fáciem tuam a púero tuo, Dómine:
body.en: O Lord, hide not thy face from thy servant

refrain.en: For I am in trouble; hear me speedily.

verse.la: Inténde ánimæ meæ, et líbera eam: propter inimícos meos éripe me.
verse.en: Draw nigh unto my soul, and redeem it; deliver me, because of mine enemies.

benedictio.la: Ad societátem cívium supernórum perdúcat nos Rex Angelórum.
benedictio.en: May He that is the Angels' King to that high realm His people bring.

source.la: Has ei laudes turba dicébat: Hosánna, benedíctus, qui venit in nómine Dómini, Rex Israël. Quam crucem mentis invidéntia príncipum Iudæórum pérpeti potúerat, quando Regem suum Christum tanta multitúdo clamábat? Sed quid fuit Dómino Regem esse Israël? Quid magnum fuit Regi sæculórum, Regem fíeri hóminum? Non enim Rex Israël Christus ad exigéndum tribútum, vel exércitum ferro armándum, hostésque visibíliter debellándos: sed Rex Israël, quod mentes regat, quod in ætérnum cónsulat, quod in regnum cælórum credéntes, sperántes, amantésque perdúcat.
source.en: These were the shouts of applause with which the crowd greeted Him, “Hosanna! Blessed is the King of Israel That cometh in the Name of the Lord!” What inward torture must the jealousy of the Jewish leaders have caused them, when they heard that great multitude hailing Christ as their King! But, for the Lord, what was it to be King of Israel? To the Eternal King what mattered it to become a King of men? And Christ is not King of Israel in the sense of monarchs who exact tribute, or arm hosts with steel to conquer enemies that are seen. But King of Israel He is, as He Who is Lord of our intellect, a Ruler Whose power shall never wane, and Who openeth a Kingdom in heaven to all such as centre in Him their faith, their hope, and their love.

body.la: Quis dabit cápiti meo aquam, et óculis meis fontem lacrimárum, et plorábo die ac nocte? quia frater propínquus supplantávit me,
body.en: O that my head were waters, and mine eyes a fountain of tears, that I might weep day and night! for my nearest brother hath supplanted me,

refrain.la: Et omnis amícus fraudulénter incéssit in me.
refrain.en: And my neighbour hath walked with slanders against me.

verse.la: Fiant viæ eórum ténebræ et lúbricum: et Angelus Dómini pérsequens eos.
verse.en: Let their way be dark and slippery, and let the Angel of the Lord persecute them.

text.la: Reliqua omittuntur, nisi Laudes separandæ sint.
text.en: Skip the rest, unless praying Lauds separately.

text.la: Profíciat, quǽsumus, Dómine, plebs tibi dicáta, piæ devotiónis afféctu: ut sacris actiónibus erudíta, quanto maiestáti tuæ fit grátior, tanto donis potióribus augeátur.
text.en: Grant, O Lord, that thy people, which are consecrated to thy service may continually increase in all godly affections: that they being duly instructed in all holy learning, may both be made the more acceptable unto thy divine majesty, and prospered more abundantly in the gifts of thy bounty.
